carrier_interface_review.finding: CPR annotations represent reduction of P450 heme states, whereas the FNS-II reaction represents reductase-bound flavin donor states. These participant identities are distinct and cannot be canceled as an exact stoichiometric join.
carrier_interface_review.evidence_boundary: All three catalytic annotations are automated. Predicted membrane and flavin-binding features are retained with evidence codes; they do not prove compatibility with an FNS-II lead.
next_requirements: Recover characterized plant CPR reference sequences for an independent full-proteome comparison.
Reconcile explicit carrier states and electron/proton accounting before constructing a coupled net equation.
Measure paired P450/CPR turnover with NADPH and authentic products, retaining P450-only, CPR-only and no-NADPH controls.
carrier_interface_review.claim_boundary: No native partnership or net conversion is established. Do not replace carrier identities with free flavin or heme, or infer missing reductase absence from a name-only inventory.

primary_assay_review.review_scope: Indexed primary results and yeast-expression/enzyme-assay methods; supplements and underlying chromatograms not independently reanalyzed
primary_assay_review.product_evidence: Retention time and tandem-mass-spectral comparison with authentic standard support apigenin identification.
primary_assay_review.substrate_stereochemistry: Not resolved by the reviewed methods wording; do not silently assert an enantiopure assay substrate.

electron_transfer.boundary: Microsomal turnover does not identify an endogenous Cannabis electron-transfer partner or establish free-flavin catalysis.

primary_assay_review.claim_boundary: Reference biochemical evidence only. The cDNA cross-reference joins the study to UniProt, not to a fully reconstructed experimental construct. Assay additives are not automatically network reactants or organic carbon seeds. Cannabis specificity, carrier regeneration and physiological flux remain unestablished.
